title: An ssh past the process scan's limit is never taken as ended
owns: app/main/remote (SA linuxSshProcesses and the other OS readers), app/main/targets/offer.ts noticer

items.text:
SA's linuxSshProcesses stops at SCAN_MAX (5000 /proc entries) without saying so. Round 3 now withdraws a seen offer when the noticer's process read no longer lists its ssh, so on a machine with about 5000 processes or more an ssh past that point is taken as ended and its offer withdrawn (or never re-offered). A read that stopped at the limit must count as incomplete: report it as 'couldn't read' (as a failed read does: nothing withdrawn) or read further. Check the Windows and macOS readers for the same. Merge note: Nothing between the two sides. The package itself leaves these open:
- SA's linuxSshProcesses stops at SCAN_MAX (5000 /proc entries) without saying so. On a machine with about 5000 processes or more, an ssh past that point could be taken as ended.
- Only CI can confirm the new tests pass on Windows and macOS (the remote.yml unit-matrix job, and npm test in ci.yml's windows and macos jobs).
- Only a real Windows+WSL run can confirm that runScript(WSL_READER) and wsl.runningNow() behave as the fakes assume.
